questions.correctLabel: It detects known secret formats such as API keys and tokens committed to a repository and alerts on them
questions.rationaleHtml:
Secret scanning searches commits for known credential patterns and alerts (and can push protection to block them).

Reference: About secret scanning - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Push protection can block a commit containing a secret before it lands. Partners can be notified to revoke leaked credentials automatically.

questions.promptHtml: What do Dependabot alerts notify a repository about?

options.label: Dependencies that have known security vulnerabilities, so maintainers can update to a patched version
Pull requests that have been open longer than a configured number of days without receiving any review
Collaborators who have not enabled two-factor authentication on their accounts within the organization

questions.correctLabel: Dependencies that have known security vulnerabilities, so maintainers can update to a patched version
questions.rationaleHtml:
Dependabot alerts flag dependencies with known vulnerabilities from the advisory database.

Reference: About Dependabot alerts - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Alerts can be paired with Dependabot security updates that auto-open fix PRs. They rely on the dependency graph and GitHub Advisory Database.

questions.promptHtml: What is the purpose of GitHub code scanning (for example with CodeQL)?

options.label: To analyze source code for security vulnerabilities and coding errors and surface them as alerts
To measure how many lines of code each contributor has added so managers can rank developer productivity
To automatically format source code according to a style guide every time a commit is pushed to a branch

questions.correctLabel: To analyze source code for security vulnerabilities and coding errors and surface them as alerts
questions.rationaleHtml:
Code scanning statically analyzes code (e.g., with CodeQL) to find security issues and bugs, reporting alerts.

Reference: About code scanning - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Code scanning can run on pull requests to catch issues before merge. It analyzes code for flaws, unlike Dependabot which checks dependencies.

questions.promptHtml: What is the purpose of a repository security advisory?

options.label: It lets maintainers privately discuss, fix, and then publish details of a vulnerability in their project
It automatically deploys a patched release to all users who have installed the affected version of the software
It permanently blocks any contributor who reported a vulnerability from opening future issues in the repository

questions.correctLabel: It lets maintainers privately discuss, fix, and then publish details of a vulnerability in their project
questions.rationaleHtml:
Security advisories provide a private space to coordinate a fix and then disclose the vulnerability responsibly.

Reference: About repository security advisories - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Advisories support private forks for collaboration and can request CVE IDs. Coordinated disclosure protects users until a fix is available.

questions.promptHtml: A maintainer wants a collaborator who can manage issues and pull requests, including labeling and closing them, but not push code. Which repository role fits best?

options.label: The Admin role, which grants full control over the repository including settings, security, and deletion
The Triage role, which allows managing issues and pull requests without granting write access to the code
The Read role, which allows viewing and cloning the repository but not managing issues or pull requests

questions.correctLabel: The Triage role, which allows managing issues and pull requests without granting write access to the code
questions.rationaleHtml:
Triage lets a user manage issues/PRs (label, assign, close) without push access to the codebase.

Reference: Repository roles for an organization - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Repo roles escalate: Read, Triage, Write, Maintain, Admin. Grant the least privilege needed. Read cannot manage issues; Admin is far more than required here.

questions.promptHtml: How do teams help manage access within a GitHub organization?

options.label: Teams group members so permissions can be granted to many people at once, and teams can be nested to mirror structure
Teams are billing units that determine how many private repositories each individual member is personally allowed to create
Teams are automated bots that review pull requests and merge them once all of the required status checks have passed

questions.correctLabel: Teams group members so permissions can be granted to many people at once, and teams can be nested to mirror structure
questions.rationaleHtml:
Teams let organizations assign repository access to groups of members and support nesting for hierarchy.

Reference: About teams - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Nested teams inherit parent access, simplifying management. Teams can also be @mentioned and set as code owners. They manage access, not billing.

questions.promptHtml: What distinguishes an organization owner from an organization member?

options.label: Owners can only view repositories, while members hold the exclusive ability to change organization-wide security settings
Owners and members have identical permissions, and the labels exist purely for display on the organization's people page
Owners have full administrative control over the organization, while members have limited access based on their granted roles

questions.correctLabel: Owners have full administrative control over the organization, while members have limited access based on their granted roles
questions.rationaleHtml:
Owners manage all org settings, billing, and members; members get access according to team and repo roles.

Reference: Roles in an organization - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Limit the number of owners to reduce risk. Members can be granted specific repository and team permissions without full org control.

questions.promptHtml: What information does an organization's audit log provide?

options.label: A record of activity and changes, such as permission updates and repository actions, for review and compliance
A ranked list of the most active contributors so administrators can reward the top performers each month
A queue of automated dependency update pull requests that are waiting for a maintainer to review and merge

questions.correctLabel: A record of activity and changes, such as permission updates and repository actions, for review and compliance
questions.rationaleHtml:
The audit log records who did what and when across the organization, supporting security and compliance reviews.

Reference: Reviewing the audit log - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Audit logs help investigate incidents and demonstrate compliance. They can often be exported or streamed to external systems for retention.

questions.promptHtml: For authenticating Git operations over HTTPS, what does GitHub recommend instead of using an account password?

options.label: Reusing the same static password across every device so that Git operations remain simple and consistent to configure
A personal access token (or other supported credential) that can be scoped and revoked independently of the account password
Disabling authentication entirely for private repositories so that trusted collaborators never need to sign in at all

questions.correctLabel: A personal access token (or other supported credential) that can be scoped and revoked independently of the account password
questions.rationaleHtml:
GitHub requires token-based authentication (PATs, SSH keys, or GitHub App tokens) instead of passwords for Git over HTTPS.

Reference: Managing your personal access tokens - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Fine-grained PATs let you scope access to specific repos and permissions and set expirations. SSH keys are another supported option for Git operations.

questions.promptHtml: What does GitHub Sponsors enable?

options.label: Automatically distributing a project's advertising revenue equally among every contributor who has ever merged a pull request
Providing financial support to open-source developers and organizations directly through their GitHub profiles
Selling proprietary closed-source licenses on a developer's behalf and handling all customer billing and support inquiries

questions.correctLabel: Providing financial support to open-source developers and organizations directly through their GitHub profiles
questions.rationaleHtml:
GitHub Sponsors lets the community fund maintainers and projects with recurring or one-time payments.

Reference: About GitHub Sponsors - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Sponsorship helps sustain open source financially. It is voluntary funding, not ad revenue sharing or license reselling.

questions.promptHtml: An enterprise wants to share code internally across all teams to encourage reuse and collaboration, following an InnerSource model. Which approach supports this?

options.label: Marking every internal project as a public repository so that external contributors can also participate and reuse the code
Restricting each project to a single private repository that only its immediate team members are permitted to view
Using internal repositories so all enterprise members can view and contribute, applying open-source practices inside the company

questions.correctLabel: Using internal repositories so all enterprise members can view and contribute, applying open-source practices inside the company
questions.rationaleHtml:
Internal repositories enable InnerSource: open-source-style collaboration visible to the whole enterprise but not the public.

Reference: GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: InnerSource brings open-source transparency and reuse inside an organization. Public exposes code externally; strictly private siloes it per team.

questions.promptHtml: Beyond apps and actions, how does the GitHub Marketplace benefit the developer community?

options.label: It provides a central place to discover both free and paid tools that integrate with and extend GitHub workflows
It hosts the only official copy of every open-source repository, replacing the need to clone projects individually
It guarantees that all listed tools are maintained by GitHub itself and therefore never require any security review

questions.correctLabel: It provides a central place to discover both free and paid tools that integrate with and extend GitHub workflows
questions.rationaleHtml:
The Marketplace centralizes discovery of community and partner tools that extend GitHub for many workflows.

Reference: About GitHub Marketplace - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Listings come from many publishers, not just GitHub, so you still evaluate trust and permissions. It aids discovery, not code hosting.

questions.promptHtml: Which statement correctly describes GitHub's paid product plans for accounts?

options.label: GitHub offers only a single paid plan, and every feature including advanced security is bundled into that one tier
GitHub offers Free, Team, and Enterprise plans, with higher tiers adding features like advanced administration and support
GitHub charges per repository created, so accounts are billed a separate recurring fee for every individual repository they own

questions.correctLabel: GitHub offers Free, Team, and Enterprise plans, with higher tiers adding features like advanced administration and support
questions.rationaleHtml:
GitHub provides tiered plans (Free, Team, Enterprise) that unlock progressively more collaboration, administration, and support features.

Reference: GitHub's plans - GitHub Docs
questions.extraHtml: Free already includes unlimited public and private repos with basic features. Higher tiers add controls like SAML SSO, advanced auditing, and support.
